assessment: The clinical interviews report seven spontaneous and six prompted accounts of saliva or drooling among 35 people. These were experiences of symptoms, with no raw-fig exposure comparison.

The supplement records dribbling, saliva buildup and different saliva consistency. One participant describes nasal symptoms at meals as distinct from their saliva experience. No dietary outcome estimate.
The pooled trial secondary analysis reports incident drooling endorsement in year two by observational treatment-start status. It supplies no raw-fig or graded symptom change.
The verified supplemental questionnaire combines salivation with several complaints. Its validation relates summary scores and provides no isolated drooling change or exposure estimate.
Thirteen early Parkinson participants and 14 controls underwent swallowing-pressure testing. Saliva is a test medium. The study gives no symptom-change or food estimate.
A retrospective series reports binary drooling by PTSD comorbidity. A second congress notice likely concerns the same study team. No dietary exposure is assigned.
The registry distinguishes self-reported drooling and dysphagia in multiple system atrophy. These are exploratory context for a distinct clinical condition, without raw fig or graded drooling change.
